items.finding: F1: Complete reviewed publication must be authenticated before ready/merge.
items.resolution: The actual guarded ready/merge main invokes the complete operative updater main read-only, independently reconstructs fourteen intended files/body/identity, validates both completed saved records against the single original parent and every blob, snapshots all controls and latest frozen inputs, and repeats authentication before ready and expected-head merge. Exclusive intents reconcile prior or uncertain attempts read-only.

items.finding: F2: Bounded identifiers inside every tracker cell.
items.resolution: One shared predicate now recognizes bounded numeric/OWR/explicit PR/canonical PR URL/known DOI identities in prose at preflight, append and postmerge, with exact-row recovery. No-space colon labels, known DOI URL queries/fragments and exact PR files/commits/checks views are covered. Extra digits/letters and unknown continuations are excluded. A standalone #1280 remains deliberately ambiguous as a mathematical problem number; explicit PR1280/PR 1280/PR#1280/PR #1280 identifies the PR.

items.finding: F3: Live destination must remain main at all phases.
items.resolution: Operative deposit preflight, updater/recovery/body synchronization, guarded ready/merge and postmerge queries now request baseRefName and reject every base other than main. Explicit phase checks also protect direct stubbed paths; a retarget after readiness prevents merge.
items.evidence: reviews/workflow_revision1/SOURCE_CHANGES.patch and REPAIR_RECEIPT.json bind both coordinators/updater/ready; three optimized-equivalent actual-code mocked suites exercise wrong/missing-base negatives and main-base positives.

items.finding: F4: Exclude the edgeless singleton from the intermediate graph scope.
items.resolution: The current manuscript and current nine-file edition explicitly require at least one graph edge where the proof uses no sinks/Kirchberg structure. Essentiality of the original finite matrix gives a nonempty no-sink/no-source graph, so the original theorem is unchanged. Both original nine-file submission and reviewed pre-repair edition/package remain preserved as history; all changed spans and intervening bytes were rebound.
